newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet sells aircraft, retires debt.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet sells aircraft, retires debt.

text.p: ValuJet Inc. said Tuesday it has sold three surplus aircraft and the pre-paid financing debt on a fourth aircraft, enabling the no-frills carrier to retire $18.7 million of aircraft bank debt.
ValuJet, based in Atlanta, said it sold the aircraft at or above the company's book value.

ValuJet resumed operations on Sept. 30 after the Federal Aviation Administration suspended it in June following the May 11 crash of flight 592 in the Florida Everglades in which all 110 people on board were killed.

"ValuJet continues to move aggressively toward further reducing surplus aircraft capacity and associated debt," said ValuJet Chief Financial Officer Steve Nevin. "We are sizing our fleet to allow moderate growth without unnecessary ownership expense."
ValuJet sold its remaining MD-83 aircraft, including its MD-80 spare parts inventory. This sale concludes the removal of the MD-80 aircraft type and supporting spares from ValuJet.
ValuJet also sold two surplus DC-9-32 aircraft, bringing its fleet to 43 DC-9 series 30 aircraft.
The airline also prepaid the debt on another DC-9-32 aircraft that ValuJet plans to sell during the first quarter.
ValuJet's stock was unchanged at $7.375 early on Nasdaq.
